Nadarzyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nadarzyn, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded in Nadarzyn in 1507; by 1921, 431 Jews made up 34% of the town, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, confirmed to exist before 1780, served as a burial ground for the broader Warsaw area; an 1829 Mazowieckie synagogue-district register documents a fence extension request. Under Communist rule, the site was afforested and remaining tombstones buried. A 2009 inspection uncovered rows of broken tombstone fragments under 40cm of sand. In 2013, an information board was installed by volunteers connected to the cmentarze-zydowskie.pl website and the 'Ulica Żydowska' project.
